subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Embroidery is best described as...
questions.explain: Embroidery decorates fabric using needle and thread to create stitched designs.

questions.q: Knitting forms fabric by...
questions.explain: Knitting builds fabric from interlocking loops of yarn worked with needles.

questions.q: Which is a synthetic (man-made) fibre?
questions.explain: Polyester is a synthetic fibre made from chemicals, unlike natural wool, silk and linen.

questions.q: Felting makes fabric by...
options: Matting and pressing fibres together with moisture and friction
questions.explain: Felting binds loose fibres into a fabric by pressing them with moisture, heat and friction.

questions.q: Which of these is a natural fibre?
questions.explain: Cotton is a natural plant fibre, while polyester, nylon and acrylic are synthetic.

questions.q: A 'mordant' is used in dyeing to...
options: Help the dye bond permanently to the fibre
questions.explain: A mordant fixes dye to the fibres so the colour is more permanent and less likely to wash out.

questions.q: Appliqué is a technique that involves...
options: Stitching shaped pieces of fabric onto a larger background cloth
questions.explain: Appliqué sews cut pieces of fabric onto a background to build up an image or pattern.

questions.q: A 'pleat' is...
options: A stitched fold pressed into fabric to shape or decorate it
questions.explain: A pleat is a fold of fabric, often pressed and stitched, used to add shape or decoration.

questions.q: Wool is a natural fibre obtained from...
questions.explain: Wool is a natural animal fibre sheared from the fleece of sheep.

questions.q: Weaving creates fabric by...
options: Interlacing warp and weft threads at right angles
Looping a single yarn with needles
questions.explain: Weaving interlaces vertical warp threads with horizontal weft threads to make cloth.

questions.q: Crochet creates fabric using...
options: A single hooked needle to interlock loops
questions.explain: Crochet uses one hooked needle to pull yarn through loops, building up the fabric.

questions.q: 'Distressing' fabric in textiles means...
options: Deliberately fraying, tearing or wearing it for effect
questions.explain: Distressing intentionally frays, tears or ages fabric to create texture and a worn look.

questions.q: In weaving, the threads held under tension on the loom that run lengthways are the...
questions.explain: The warp threads run lengthways and are held taut on the loom while the weft is woven across them.

questions.q: In a repeating textile print, the single unit that repeats is called the...
questions.explain: The motif is the design unit that is repeated across the fabric to form an all-over pattern.

questions.q: Which textile designer is famous for nature-inspired patterns of the Arts and Crafts movement?
questions.explain: William Morris designed richly patterned, nature-based textiles and wallpapers in the Arts and Crafts style.

questions.q: Block printing on fabric works by...
options: Pressing an inked carved block onto the cloth
questions.explain: Block printing presses a raised, inked carved block onto fabric to repeat a motif.

questions.q: What is tie-dye?
options: Binding fabric tightly before dyeing so bound areas resist the dye
questions.explain: In tie-dye, fabric is tied or bound so the bound parts resist the dye, creating patterns.

questions.q: 'Smocking' is a technique that...
options: Gathers fabric with stitches to create decorative texture and stretch
questions.explain: Smocking gathers and stitches fabric to make a flexible, decoratively textured surface.

questions.q: Bonding (interfacing) fabric with heat from an iron usually relies on...
options: A glue web or adhesive that melts
questions.explain: Bondaweb and fusible interfacing carry a heat-activated adhesive that melts to join fabrics.

questions.q: Which natural fibre comes from the cocoon of the silkworm?
questions.explain: Silk is a natural protein fibre produced by silkworms when they spin their cocoons.

questions.q: Batik is a textile technique that uses what to resist dye?
questions.explain: In batik, hot wax is applied to fabric so the waxed areas resist the dye.

questions.q: 'Devore' (burnout) is a technique that...
options: Uses a chemical to dissolve fibres and leave a sheer pattern
questions.explain: Devore applies a chemical paste that burns away certain fibres, leaving a sheer patterned effect.
